contradictions.why: Buy cyclicals while they lose money, before the turn (also DRU2-C069 margin mean reversion, DRU2-C076 'a lot of countercyclical stuff'). Rbuy5 buys once trends start up, and Rbuy6 says not in the zero inning. The card records no countercyclical scope. Item 8 (play the turn vs trend) is open and does not cover it.

Expects a 2023 recession (DRU2-C006) yet is short fixed income; DRU2-C022's note says the own-Treasuries playbook did not work in 2022 because inflation was above 5% (DRU2-C004/C005). Card item 11 limits Rbuy1 only by the fat-pitch test and gives no inflation condition.
A 15-20% index rally in a post-bubble bear market is a trigger to go short. Rbuy5 buys a rising trend. Likely a different scope (index short in a bear market) but the card does not record it.
Bought tech near the 2000 top against his own view, a mistake; card section 4 item 7 already treats the 2000 re-buy as emotion, a different scope from reasoned re-entry.

notes: Not buy/price/sell, so outside the contradiction check, but worth fixing on the card: DRU2-C049 says waiting two or three WEEKS loses 60-70% of the move, while Rproc8 (DRU4-C032) says two or three MONTHS. Same measure, number differs far beyond 20%; check the DRU4 quote.
DRU2-C036 gives 12-18 months as his general horizon, not only for shorts. That weakens card section 4 item 3 ('different scope': shorts 12-18 vs investing 18-24). DRU2-C070 says 18 or 24 months.

DRU2-C050/C052/C064 put on very large positions at once. Card Rsize6 says start with a third; card section 4 item 5 records 'in big right away' only as a 'sometimes' exception (size part, outside the check).
Price part: still no rule. DRU2-C083 (cheap against the outlook one or two years out) and DRU2-C001 (de-rated 60-70%) are views only.
